metadata.notes: The first stage of a real, well-documented two-stage frying technique for potato specifically (double-fried French fries/chips) — a genuinely different verb from FRY, not a parameter on it, because it produces a genuinely different, unfinished intermediate result (pale, soft, cooked through but not crisp), not the same dish reached differently. requiredToolCapabilities/requiredIngredientCapabilities identical to FRY's (same isFryingVessel check, same oil) — the two verbs differ in temperature band and resulting state, not equipment; see fry.json's toolCapabilityNote for the 2026-08-14 id-to-capability fix applied identically here. Scoped to potato only (isParFryable, not shared with egg/garlic's isFryable) since this is a specific, sourced potato technique, not a general claim about frying anything twice.
metadata.sourcesNote: 145-165°C: Thermoworks' documented double-fry method (https://blog.thermoworks.com/golden-crisp-french-fries/) cites 325°F/163°C for 4-5 minutes as the par-fry stage — starch granules swell/gelatinize and dissolve into a more robust surface layer at this lower temperature, which is what the FINISHING fry (data/actions/fry.json's oilTempC, ~191°C cited by the same source) then crisps. Confidence: commonly_cited_unverified (a well-regarded food-science-literate source, not itself peer-reviewed) — matching this repo's existing confidence-tier discipline (see oil.json's IOC citation for the same tier). The peer-reviewed backing for WHY a two-temperature approach works at all is Kalogianni & Smith, "Effect of frying variables on French fry properties," International Journal of Food Science and Technology 48(4):758-770 (2013), https://doi.org/10.1111/ijfs.12024 (confidence: standard_reference) — verified via direct lookup 2026-08-13, not recalled from training data.
metadata.restNote: The same source states fries should REST at least 10 minutes between the two frying stages before the finishing fry — a real, necessary part of the technique (lets residual heat/moisture redistribute before the second, hotter stage). This repo has no REST verb (ROADMAP.md's 'More common technique verbs' still lists it as open, closed narrowly only for post-cook egg carryover via SHOCK) — named honestly as a real gap rather than silently skipped or faked via an unrelated verb: a recipe using PAR_FRY then FRY today has no way to express the rest interval between them at all, only the two cooking steps themselves.
metadata.thicknessNote: Real technique (same source) specifies ~1/4 inch (~6mm) stick thickness as achieving 'an optimal crust-to-filling ratio' — connects directly to data/actions/cut.json's 'shape' parameter (already a real state on potato: sliced/diced/julienne/chopped/minced) but this schema does not compute or require any particular shape/thickness before PAR_FRY is legal, nor adjust durationSeconds for it — see potato.json's fryingScienceNote for the fuller citation on why piece size genuinely matters here and isn't modeled numerically.
metadata.loadNote: The same source also notes adding too many pieces at once drops oil temperature excessively, recommending frying only about half a batch at a time to hold the target oilTempC — a real, batch-size/thermal-mass interaction, PARTIALLY addressed 2026-08-14: src/place.ts now models the oil's own heat capacity for real (advanceTempSeconds, oil.json's specificHeatJPerKgK), closing the 'no concept of oil's own heat capacity' half of this gap named when this note was first written. What's still genuinely unmodeled: place.ts has no concept of a target instance's own thermal mass being added to (and cooling) the oil — dropping a batch of cold fries into hot oil is a real heat-exchange event between two masses, and nothing here computes the resulting temperature drop or how many 'target instances' constitute one applyAction call's batch. Named as the real remainder, not silently implied closed by the heat-capacity half that IS now real.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true at the DATA/INVENTORY level only (no duplication, no engine error) — same caveat as fry.json's identical flag: re-running this on an already-par-fried or already-finished potato risks over-cooking it, a real physical risk this schema-level flag can't paper over.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): same reasoning as fry.json — a real, elapsed-time thermal process in oil, matching the paper's 'heating' example. Not yet wired to the place.ts/HEAT_PLACE readiness check (named as a deliberate, close follow-up in recipe-runner.ts's own top doc comment) — applyAction executes it atomically today.
metadata.maxDurationSecondsNote: Reused directly from this action's own already-cited durationSeconds.numericRange.max (600s) rather than a new number — the top of an already-established real range doubles as a reasonable timeout ceiling; see PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md TICKET 2's acceptance criteria ("do not copy the paper's numbers") and this action's own durationSeconds parameter for the reasoning behind 600s itself.

verification.description: Fries turned blonde/pale and soft — cooked through, but NOT browned or crisp (that's FRY's job, second stage)

hazards.note: Hot oil splatter; pan-surface contact burn risk — same hazard as FRY
